data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A small team building a research tool with active learning loops should build a custom, minimal experiment tracker where the tracker acts as the causal controller, rather than adopting an existing tool which treats experimentation as passive observation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team's research does not involve real-time parameter mutation based on intermediate results (i.e., it is purely observational).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"An existing platform offers a native, low-latency webhook or streaming API that allows external controllers to modify running experiments without schema violation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain the correctness of the custom state machine, risking data integrity more than using a flawed wrapper.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Control Theory Boundary: Existing tools abstract the experiment loop into a 'log-and-observe' workflow, severing the causal link between metric evaluation and parameter adjustment.
